text:
Ava (AE): Quick sync - prospect's vendor team opened a CAIQ thread. Two asks: clarify key custody across deployment modes, and provide a short attestation about raw prompt retention. They want a concise artifact for procurement.

Diego (Security): TL;DR: Hosted = Redwood-managed KMS by default; Hosted BYOK available (AWS/GCP KMS + HSM options). Dedicated = customer-configurable KMS or Redwood-managed if contracted. Private = customer-managed only. I'll write a 1-paragraph custody statement.

Sam (Solutions Eng): For logs: default hosted operational logs retained 30 days. We have a POC mode with ephemeral logs (no raw prompt persistence). We can also push audit logs to customer projects or support log export.

Rachel (Vendor Risk): Also need clarity on whether Redwood staff can ever read plaintext in Hosted mode and what controls are in place for emergency access. A short sentence and proof (e.g., audit sample) would help move the review.

Diego (Security): Emergency access: runtime decryption occurs on serving nodes; access to plaintext requires approved access tickets, RBAC approvals, and is logged with an immutable audit trail. For BYOK customers, keys remain under customer control; Redwood never retains plaintext keys.

Sam (Solutions Eng): Snippet you can paste into CAIQ responses:

```
Key Custody: Redwood defaults to provider-managed key material for Hosted deployments, with enterprise BYOK options (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, HSM). Dedicated may be configured to use customer KMS; Private deployments require customer-managed keys. BYOK keys are not stored by Redwood and are fully controlled by the customer.

Data Retention & Logs: Operational logs are retained by default for 30 days. For proof-of-concept engagements we can enable ephemeral logging to avoid storage of raw prompts. Audit log export to customer-managed storage is available.

Access & Emergency Procedures: Any access to decrypted data is gated by RBAC, documented approval workflows, and recorded in audit logs. Separation of duties prevents ad-hoc plaintext access; customers may request audit extracts for vendor reviews.
```

Diego (Security): I'll attach: (1) one-page CAIQ mapping, (2) BYOK integration diagram, (3) sanitized rotation/audit sample. Uploading now.

redwood-ops-bot: Uploaded: https://internal.redwood/drive/ca iq-mapping-byo-1821.pdf (ca iq-mapping-byo-1821.pdf)

Ava (AE): Rachel, will that be enough for initial intake?

Rachel (Vendor Risk): Looks good. Rotation entries sample would be ideal for final sign-off but initial pass should accept the attestation and the diagram. If you can include a 1-sentence attestation signed by security, that'll speed approval.

Diego (Security): Adding attestation line to the CAIQ mapping doc and will post a sanitized rotation screenshot. ETA 16:30 PT. :white_check_mark:

Ava (AE): Great — I'll send the packet once Diego confirms. Thanks folks.
